children: , the cloud, commerce and AI-infrastructure giant, chose a pragmatic lane in the AI-safety debate: push for tougher testing and safeguards without putting the brakes on development. Shares climbed approximately 1.6% to $255.09, based on the latest price shown in the chart, extending the market's appetite for Amazon's sprawling AI opportunity.

The company is backing stronger cooperation between industry and government, but it stopped short of supporting a coordinated pause in AI development. That matters because Amazon has chips on nearly every square of the AI board: proprietary models, Alexa, its AGI ambitions and Bedrock, where AWS customers can tap models from multiple providers. The message is straightforward make AI safer, but keep shipping products and filling data centers.

The economics make that balancing act increasingly important. AWS generated $42.2 billion last quarter, while Amazon said both its AI and semiconductor businesses have surpassed $25 billion in annualized revenue run rates. Yet free cash flow swung to a $7.6 billion trailing outflow as infrastructure spending exploded. The chart adds a valuation reality check: at $255.09, Amazon trades roughly 2.55% above its $248.74 GF Value estimate. Investors are already paying slightly above that benchmark, putting even more pressure on Amazon to turn its enormous AI spending into durable growth without sacrificing trust.

title: Amazon Rallies While Drawing Its Own AI Safety Line
